assumptions: Same model as H-SMT-01; two encodings: word-level QF_BV and bit-blasted pure SAT.

Adaptive timeout per encoding: 8x its previous solve time at the same r, clamped to [min, max]; a (r, k) point with every instance timing out ends that r for that encoding; an r with no solved k ends the encoding. Encodings alternate at every point so the budget is shared.
Growth rates are least-squares slopes of log2(median solve seconds) vs k over solved points with solve time >= 50 ms (to exclude fixed overhead); extrapolated crossovers are heuristic.
Brute force: single thread, generic reduced-round midstate path.
Solver statistics are Z3's internal counters (sat conflicts, decisions).
baseline: Single-thread brute force; measured slope of log2(hashes to first hit) vs k (expected 1).
conclusion: REDUCED-ROUND ONLY: deviations were detected only for reduced-round variants. These say nothing about full 64-round SHA-256/SHA-256d and give no mining advantage; full-round configurations (where tested) showed no deviation. 129 solver runs over encodings ["qfbv", "bitblast-sat"]; frontier (first point where every instance timed out): bitblast-sat r=8 k=4, qfbv r=8 k=16. qfbv r=6: solve time grows 2^0.34 per target bit (se 0.18, 3 points) vs brute force 2^0.92. qfbv r=8: solve time grows 2^0.39 per target bit (se 0.78, 3 points) vs brute force 2^1.13. bitblast-sat r=6: solve time grows 2^0.60 per target bit (se 0.18, 5 points) vs brute force 2^0.92. qfbv: insufficient contrast between size and time growth to attribute the bottleneck. bitblast-sat: insufficient contrast between size and time growth to attribute the bottleneck. Time budget of 900 s exhausted; grid incomplete.

dataset.description: `instances` random headers per point from SplitMix64::stream(seed, instance).

errata.note: Solve times are heavy-tailed: at 6 to 8 rounds an instance either solves in 0.1 to 0.5 s with about 100 to 200 conflicts or runs past the 2 to 4 s timeout with 15k to 40k conflicts. The adaptive timeout (8x the previous solve time, minimum 2 s) is too short for that, so the reported frontiers and growth-rate fits reflect the timeout, not scaling, and the encoding difference at 8 rounds is not supported. Measured statuses, times and the 4-round result stand.

hypothesis: For some round count r, the cost of SAT/SMT nonce search on r-round SHA-256d grows more slowly in the target size k than brute force (factor 2 per bit), or beats brute force outright.
methodology: Grid over encodings x rounds x target bits with several random headers per point, adaptive timeouts and a global time budget. Each solve reports build time, solve time, DAG size, solver counters and (once per r) the bit-blasted CNF size. Timeouts are diagnosed by comparing growth of model size and growth of solve time across r.
name: Scaling of SAT/SMT nonce search with rounds and target difficulty
null_hypothesis: Solver cost per additional target bit is at least that of brute force, and the solver is never faster in absolute terms.

diagnosis.verdict: insufficient contrast between size and time growth to attribute the bottleneck
insufficient contrast between size and time growth to attribute the bottleneck

reproduction.method: not run in-process for this kind; use `bmr research reproduce <id>`

verification.method: every solver nonce recomputed with sha256-core (midstate) and verification::independent (full header); unsat answers checked against brute force
